title: Majority of Australians who report penicillin allergy not truly allergic
paragraphs: The majority of Australians who report a penicillin allergy are not truly allergic, prompting the peak body for immunologists to change its guidelines in a bid to reduce hospital stays and tackle antimicrobial resistance.
Penicillin, one of the most commonly prescribed antibiotics in Australia, was thought to cause allergies in 10% of Australians, or about 2.8 million people.
But the latest evidence shows up to 90% of those reporting a penicillin allergy do not have one.
